messages.subject: gpagen coding error?
messages.body_plain:
I've checked this on a couple of datasets now.

The 'shapes' gpagen$coords produces are not unit size. They vary. The mean of gpagen$coords [apply(gpagen$coords, c(1,2), mean)] is however a configuration of unit size. My guess is that these two things are related within the function. But I think the priorities are backwards. The observations need to be shapes, ie of unit size. The mean configuration maybe doesn't need to be a shape because it is not actually a specimen (i.e., it's not really in the shape space of the observations).

On the other hand, if you take an array of unit size configurations and compute the mean shape with geomorph (mshape), the mean configuration is less than unit size.

The mshape result makes sense. In my experience, there is always some shrinkage when computing a shape mean. You just live with it because the alternative, where the mean shape is rescaled to unit size, does not allow for mean=0 procrustes residuals.

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] gpagen coding error?
messages.body_plain:
David,

This is not a coding error. The reason for this observation is that in gpagen, the default is Projection=TRUE. That is, following standard GM practice, shapes are aligned using GPA and then projected orthogonally to Tangent Space. This projection results in slight differences in perceived sizes in tangent space (See Rohlf 1999 and others on the relationship of shape space and tangent space and how this is linked through Csize).

As a simple example try the following:

library(geomorph)

  data(plethodon)

  Y.gpa1 <- gpagen(plethodon$land,PrinAxes=FALSE,Proj=F)

  gpagen(Y.gpa1$coords,Proj=F)$Csize

  Y.gpa2 <- gpagen(plethodon$land,PrinAxes=FALSE,Proj=T)

  gpagen(Y.gpa2$coords,Proj=F)$Csize

Note that in Y.gpa1, there is no orthogonal projection. In this case the sizes are all equal to 1.0.  However, now your shapes are in the curved hemispherical shape space, making some statistical analyses challenging (ie, those methods that require linear statistics, which is a considerable swath of multivariate statistics).

The second example, shapes are aligned and projected into Tangent Space. The sizes vary slightly, but the shapes are in a linear space appropriate for the types of statistics we typically utilize to compare shapes.

Dean

messages.subject: buildtemplate coding problem
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am new to the geomorph package and am having trouble with the buildtemplate function. I am trying to use the geomorph package to analyze the shape characteristics of the calcanei (heel foot bones) of different foot types. I have been able to read in a ".ply" file that contains a 3d mesh of the bone as well as a matrix of landmark points that I have selected externally. My issue has been with the repeatability of the build template function when I ask the function to select 200 more surface semilandmarks. When I read in the same file with the same landmark points and ask the function to create the surface semilandmarks, the build template function gives me a different series of semilandmarks each time. I am not sure if this is an inherent property of the function causing some variability with the semilandmark points, or if I am using the function incorrectly. I have been able to use the template built from this function effectively in the digitize surface function and have done some Principal component analysis with results that are similar but not identical when using the same data. Additionally, I am not attempting to use the curve sliders, just the surface semilandmarks for this case. Any help on the buildtemplate function or further explanation would be great. I am currently calling the function as follows,

buildtemplate(get(bone_surface_name),get(bone_landmark_name),200, ptsize=0.5, center=TRUE)

where I had previously assigned the variables "bone_surface_name" and "bone_landmark_name" to their respective ".ply" and matrix files using the read.ply and as.matrix functions.

Thanks,
Erik

messages.body_plain:
I have checked this and confirm your observation:

lmk <- as.matrix(read.csv("app01_Right_calcaneuslandmarks.csv", sep=" ", header=F))
ply <- read.ply("app01_Right_calcaneus.ply")

temp1 <- buildtemplate(ply, lmk, 200, center = F)
temp2 <- buildtemplate(ply, lmk, 200, center = F)
temp3 <- buildtemplate(ply, lmk, 200, center = F)

shade3d(ply, col="grey")
points3d(lmk, col="red", size=10)
points3d(temp1, col="blue", size=10)
points3d(temp2, col="green", size=10)
points3d(temp3, col="black", size=10)

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-Cq0ZRUw60qs/V5lkLOU8suI/AAAAAAAACJE/mHOrehZw4ikkNjch0eTCzN_Ut7OUT2B9wCLcB/s1600/buildtemplate.tiff>

I have also checked with a few other datasets and found the same. There I must apologise but my original comment was incorrect, no the templates will not always be the same. As I re-familiarise myself with the function (which I worked on a long while ago), I see now that in a 3D case, with such a large point cloud, and only 100 iterations allowed, the function kmeans will always find a slightly different result. But the results are never very different.

Emma
